fig1: Figure 1  Model structure and assessment design

A: Revised SUEIHCDR transmission subsystem, with vaccination and behavioural protection separated and recovered states grouped for readability. Variant-dependent leak pathways permit infection from vaccine-protected and selected recovered pools. Dashed arrows represent observation of progression fluxes, not additional state transitions. Admissions are modelled through infectious outflow; detailed clinical occupancy pathways are outside this subsystem. The supplementary equations specify which recovered groups can be reinfected. B: Distinct assessments applied to the same model family. The sequence organizes the questions asked; passing an earlier assessment does not establish validity for the next use. Source: implemented model equations and study protocols. All schematic elements were newly drawn.
fig2: Figure 2  Serological calibration and residual agreement

A, C, E: Blood-donor seroprevalence and model ever-infected shares before commercial-survey calibration (L3) and after calibration (L3B), sampled at the same survey dates. B, D, F: Corresponding model-minus-donor differences; shading marks the declared tolerance from -0.10 to +0.20 in population share. The band is a diagnostic tolerance, not a confidence interval. Donor observations are regional in 2020–2021 and statewide in 2022, and do not directly measure county immunity. Commercial serology informed calibration and is excluded from these panels. The late residuals reveal a limitation concealed by the pooled pass rule. Source: Phase 17B serology_check.csv, validation rows only.
fig3: Figure 3  Continuous reconstruction over both scenario periods

A, C, E: October-start behaviour period, 3 October 2020–2 April 2021. B, D, F: December-start vaccination period, 12 December 2020–3 December 2021. Coloured curves show continuous model admissions without later E/I boundary corrections. Black points show observed weekly mean admissions at week midpoints, restricted to complete reporting weeks wholly inside each period. Vertical scales are shared within a county. Annotations give saved comparable-week total ratios and peak shifts in days; positive shifts mean a later model peak. Different initial states and period-specific retrospectively estimated inputs prevent interpretation as an isolated initialization test. Source: Phase 18 baseline daily paths, reconstruction summaries and corrected Phase 15 admissions.
fig4: Figure 4  Exposed and infectious state corrections

Multipliers applied at successive overlapping-window boundaries for exposed states (A, C, E) and infectious states (B, D, F). A value of one leaves the carried state unchanged; values below one reduce it. The horizontal axis identifies the beginning of the fitted window, 56 days before its issue date, rather than the forecast origin. Shading marks December 2020 on that first-window-date axis. The primary L3B reporting-delay chain is shown. Corrections describe the estimation procedure and are not direct measurements of infection or evidence identifying a unique cause of reconstruction drift. Source: Phase 17B params_states.csv; plotted dates and the December geometric-mean summary use the same definition.
fig5: Figure 5  Scenario bracketing on original and wholly future grids

A: The historical reporting-index coverage of the minimum-to-maximum P0–P4 envelope. B: Post hoc coverage by wholly future calendar week in the primary chain; every included week starts after the issue date. Missing observations and absent forecasts are omitted, without filling. C: An ordinary primary origin illustrates why reporting index h = 1 is partly elapsed; the first future week ordinarily maps to h = 2. The San Diego 22 May 2021 calendar exception is documented in Section S10. Dashed lines mark the historical 50% reference; the scenario envelope has no nominal probability level. New re-scoring changes the percentages but leaves bracketing poor. Sources: saved Phase 18B v2 weekly outputs; future_week_by_lead.csv.
fig6: Figure 6  Conditional vaccination timing and admissions

A–C: Saved daily model admission intensity under baseline vaccination, doses shifted 28 days earlier and substitution of San Francisco's per-capita pace. San Francisco's own pace equals its baseline and is omitted as a separate curve. D: Complete-period admissions changes when subsequent dose flows are set to zero; the initial protected share is retained. E: Changes under earlier doses and pace substitution, using the same colours as the trajectories. SD, LA and SF denote the three counties. Points show the primary chain; whiskers span selected sensitivity chains, not confidence intervals. Transmission and behavioural inputs remain fixed, so all contrasts are conditional model responses. Source: Phase 18 daily and summary outputs, 12 December 2020–3 December 2021.
figS1: Figure S1  Admissions errors and paired comparisons

A–C: Saved mean admissions errors over reporting-week indices 1–3, averaged across eligible origins, for the sequential mechanistic models and simple comparators. Blue identifies L3B and green the testing-linked L3T sensitivity. D: Paired L3B-minus-ARIMA mean-error differences with the saved 95% four-origin moving-block-bootstrap intervals, in admissions/day. The displayed numerical intervals use a common horizontal scale; zero marks equal mean error. The intervals were not recalculated. Overlap with zero does not establish equivalence. All versions reused historical observations during adaptive development. Source: saved model summaries and Phase 17B criteria.json; 110 eligible San Diego origins and 114 in each other county.
figS2: Figure S2  Reconstruction and scenario sensitivities

A: October-start model/observed admission-total ratios for primary L3B and testing-linked L3T. Shading marks the original 0.8–1.2 total-ratio tolerance. Both versions exceed its upper limit in all three counties. B: Coverage over reporting indices 1–4 in the three saved origin-specific projection chains; all remain below the declared 50% criterion. Delay-zero and delay-one chains use different calendar targets at the same index and are therefore not matched-calendar comparisons. Source: Phase 18 and Phase 19 reconstruction summaries and Phase 18B v2 envelope_e1.csv. Points summarize saved outputs; no new significance test is implied.
figS3: Figure S3  Decisions depend on diagnostic tolerances

A: Fraction of the 21 common donor dates within each band for L3B. Horizontal lines indicate required fractions of one-half, two-thirds and four-fifths. Bands are arithmetic model-minus-survey differences, not confidence intervals. B: Joint reconstruction decisions for each combination of total and peak tolerance, retaining the original serology rule. Outlines mark the original ±20% and 14-day combination. This post hoc grid reclassifies saved trajectories; it does not propagate parameter uncertainty. Sources: serology_threshold_sensitivity.csv and reconstruction_threshold_sensitivity.csv.
figS4: Figure S4  Fixed progression timing and variable admissions scaling

A: Analytic E/I outflow kernel for a new entrant to E, with mean 12.1 days and standard deviation 8.66 days. The kernel is implied by fixed model rates, rather than estimated from patient-level admission delays. B–D: Weekly fitted admissions multiplier q over October 2020–December 2021, spanning the two overlapping reconstruction periods. q is constant within each fit, changes across stitched weeks and is held at its issue-specific value in each projection. These trajectories do not separately identify clinical severity. Sources: admissions_kernel.csv and admissions_q_history.csv.
